_meta.description: BJJ Technique Taxonomy - Research-based seed data for MatMentor
sources: John Danaher - Enter the System / New Wave / Go Further Faster series
BJJ World, BJJ Heroes, BJJ Equipment competition analysis
Academy curricula: Jay Pages JJMMA, Synergy BJJ, BJJ Foundation

domains.name: Standing / Takedowns
domains.description: Taking the fight to the ground. Danaher Step 1: Remove opponent's ability to use legs for power generation.
domains.danaher_mapping: Feet to Floor / Standing to Ground series

domains.name: Guard Play
domains.description: Bottom position with legs as primary weapons. Sweeps, submissions, and retention from guard. Danaher Step 2 obstacle: opponent must get past the legs.
domains.danaher_mapping: New Wave: Open Guard, Half Guard, Closed Guard / GFF: Closed Guard, Half Guard, Open Guard, Guard Retention

domains.name: Guard Passing
domains.description: Getting past opponent's legs to achieve a dominant top position. Statistically, securing a guard pass gives 99.6% win probability.
domains.danaher_mapping: New Wave: No-Gi Guard Passing / GFF: Passing the Guard, Half Guard Passing & Dynamic Pins

domains.name: Positional Control & Escapes
domains.description: Maintaining dominant pins (side control, mount, back, knee-on-belly) and escaping from inferior positions. Danaher Steps 3-4: hierarchy of pins graded by striking/submission ability.
domains.belt_emphasis: White belt = survival, Blue belt = escapes (Ribeiro)
domains.ribeiro_mapping: Chapter 2: White Belt - Survival / Chapter 3: Blue Belt - Escapes
domains.danaher_mapping: New Wave: Positional Escapes, Submission Escapes / GFF: Pin Escapes & Turtle Escapes

domains.name: Submissions
domains.description: Finishing techniques: chokes, joint locks, and leg locks. Competition data: 53% chokes, ~24% arm attacks, ~23% leg attacks.
domains.danaher_mapping: Enter the System series (Leg Locks, Back Attacks, Front Headlocks, Triangles, Kimuras, Armbars)

positions.name: Standing
positions.description: Both fighters on feet. Entry point for all grappling exchanges.

positions.name: Closed Guard
positions.description: Bottom player's legs wrapped around opponent's waist, ankles locked. Classic BJJ position.
positions.ribeiro_coverage: Purple Belt chapter - vs kneeling and standing opponents
positions.danaher_coverage: New Wave: Closed Guard / GFF: Closed Guard

positions.name: Open Guard
positions.description: Bottom player's legs not locked around opponent. Includes collar-sleeve, seated guard. Most common guard for sweeping in IBJJF.

positions.name: Half Guard
positions.description: Bottom player controls one of opponent's legs between theirs. Includes standard, lockdown, Z-guard, deep half, butterfly half.
positions.danaher_coverage: New Wave: Half Guard / GFF: Half Guard

positions.name: Butterfly Guard
positions.description: Seated guard with both feet as hooks inside opponent's thighs. Strong sweeping position.

positions.name: De La Riva Guard
positions.description: Open guard with one leg hooking behind opponent's lead leg. One of the best guards for sweeping per IBJJF data. Includes reverse DLR.
positions.ribeiro_coverage: Purple Belt chapter - DLR and Reverse DLR

positions.name: Spider Guard
positions.description: Gi-based open guard using sleeve grips with feet on opponent's biceps. Includes lasso variation.

positions.name: X-Guard / Single Leg X
positions.description: Guard with legs forming an X shape under opponent. Includes full X-guard and single-leg X (Ashi Garami entry). Strong sweeping and leg lock entry position.
positions.ribeiro_coverage: Brown Belt chapter (passing), Purple Belt chapter (playing)

positions.name: 50/50 Guard
positions.description: Symmetrical leg entanglement. One of the best guards for sweeping per IBJJF data. Also a leg lock entry.

positions.name: Turtle
positions.description: Defensive position on hands and knees, protecting neck. Common transition position.
positions.danaher_coverage: GFF: Strangles & Turtle Breakdowns / Pin Escapes & Turtle Escapes

positions.name: Side Control
positions.description: Dominant pin across opponent's chest. Includes traditional, kesa gatame (scarf hold), reverse kesa, and north-south variations.
positions.ribeiro_coverage: White Belt (survival), Blue Belt (escapes), Black Belt (submissions from)

positions.name: North-South
positions.description: Head-to-head pin position. Strong control, limited but effective submissions.

positions.name: Knee on Belly
positions.description: Dominant position with knee on opponent's torso. Mobile, high-pressure pin. Transition point to mount or back.

positions.name: Mount
positions.description: Sitting on opponent's torso. Includes low mount, high mount, S-mount, and technical mount. Second-best position in Danaher hierarchy.
positions.ribeiro_coverage: White Belt (survival), Blue Belt (escapes), Black Belt (submissions from)

positions.name: Back Control
positions.description: Controlling opponent from behind with hooks and/or body triangle. Best position in Danaher hierarchy. Produces most submissions in competition (45% of IBJJF 2023 subs were from back).
positions.ribeiro_coverage: White Belt (survival), Blue Belt (escapes), Black Belt (submissions from)
positions.danaher_coverage: Enter the System: Back Attacks (Straight Jacket System)

positions.name: Front Headlock / Turtle Top
positions.description: Controlling opponent's head from the front while they are turtled or on hands and knees. Gateway to guillotines, darces, anacondas.

positions.name: Inside Guard (Top)
positions.description: Top position inside opponent's guard. The passer's perspective. Starting point for all guard passing sequences.

positions.name: Leg Entanglements (Ashi Garami)
positions.description: Leg-on-leg control positions for attacking lower body submissions. Danaher system: outside ashi (least control) to inside sankaku (max control). Includes SLX, 50/50, honey hole/inside sankaku, outside ashi, cross ashi.

positions.name: Crucifix
positions.description: Controlling opponent with arms trapped, one by legs, one by arms. High-control submission position.

ribeiro_progression.white_belt: Survival - defensive posture from mount, side control, back, knee-on-belly
ribeiro_progression.blue_belt: Escapes - back escapes, mount escapes, side control escapes, knee-on-belly escape, submission defense (armbar, triangle, guillotine, footlock, kimura)
ribeiro_progression.purple_belt: Guard - closed guard (vs kneeling/standing), butterfly guard, spider guard, cross-grip guard, De La Riva guard, sit-up guard, reverse DLR, half guard
ribeiro_progression.brown_belt: Guard Passing - passes for butterfly, spider, cross-grip, DLR, sit-up, reverse DLR, inverted, x-guard, half guard
ribeiro_progression.black_belt: Submissions - from back, mount, side control, turtle, half guard, guard

four_step_system: 3. Hierarchy of pins (side control → knee on belly → mount → back)
danaher_systems.positional_hierarchy: Standing → Takedown → Guard Top → Pass → Side Control → Knee on Belly → Mount → Back Control → Submission

top_submissions_nogi_adcc_2023.5: Leg locks general (28-30% of all finishes)

key_insights: 40% of back takes come during guard passing attempts
Close-distance passes succeed 2x more than long-distance
51% of submissions from top, 49% from bottom
Chokes = 53% of finishes, arm locks ~24%, leg locks ~23%

ibjjf_leg_lock_legality.purple: Straight ankle lock only (gi), calf slicer added at some events
ibjjf_leg_lock_legality.brown_to_black: Straight ankle lock, kneebar, toe hold, calf slicer (gi). Heel hooks legal in no-gi at brown/black.
ibjjf_leg_lock_legality.adcc_nogi: All leg locks legal at all levels
